mainTopic: The fast-day שליח ציבור, the 24 ברכות, and how the order differs in the מקדש
overview: This amud finishes רבי יהודה's description of the right שליח ציבור for a תענית ציבור: his house is free of sin, and he had a clean name from his youth. A פסוק in ירמיה is read as describing an unworthy שליח ציבור, whose voice ה׳ 'hates.' The גמרא then asks how the משנה can count six added ברכות when it lists seven endings. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the first ending is the regular ברכה of גואל ישראל, only made longer. A ברייתא describes the order: after each ברכה the people answer אמן, and the כהנים blow, switching between תקיעה and תרועה. In the מקדש there is no אמן, based on a פסוק in נחמיה. Instead the people answer ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד. When רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון used the מקדש order in their towns, the חכמים said it belonged only at the שערי מזרח and the הר הבית. A second version of the same ברייתא repeats this, and the amud ends as רבי אדא דמן יפו begins explaining why רבי יהודה omits זכרונות and שופרות, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Aren't two of the qualities the same thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה lists both 'burdened with children and has nothing' and 'his house is empty,' since they seem to mean the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't 'burdened with children and has nothing' the same as 'his house is empty'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's list of qualities for the fast-day שליח ציבור by pointing out that two of them seem to repeat each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone with a family to feed and no money has, by definition, an empty house. So listing both seems repetitive. The גמרא assumes every phrase must add something, so it demands an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't that the same as? (used to point out that two things look identical)
Burdened, meaning someone with a family depending on him
His house is empty

phrases.english: Isn't 'burdened with children and has nothing'
the same as 'his house is empty'?
phrases.notes: Quoting the second quality, which seems identical

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ מְטוּפָּל וְאֵין לוֹ הַיְינוּ בֵּיתוֹ רֵיקָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from earlier on the daf of רבי יהודה's list of qualities for the fast-day שליח ציבור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two items in the list seem to repeat each other, and a list should not contain an empty repetition.

steps.title: His house is empty of sin
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that 'his house is empty' means his house is free of sin, not free of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This means his house is empty of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge by giving 'his house is empty' a new meaning: his home is clean of any wrongdoing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the two phrases describe different things. 'Burdened and has nothing' is about being poor, which makes him pray from the heart. 'His house is empty' is about being morally clean. So there is no repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin, a transgression

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This means that his house is empty of sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא זֶהוּ שֶׁבֵּיתוֹ רֵיקָם מִן הָעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a phrase so it no longer repeats the other phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'His house is empty' means he is poor, which is the same as 'burdened and has nothing.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'His house is empty' means free of sin, which is a separate quality.

steps.title: Meaning of 'his youth was becoming'
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'his youth was becoming' means he never had a bad reputation when he was young.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And his youth was becoming' — אביי said: This is someone who never got a bad name in his youth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains another quality on רבי יהודה's list. אביי says it refers to a person who had a clean reputation even as a young man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being good now is not enough. The שליח ציבור should not have a past that people remember badly. This matters because the whole community is relying on him to speak for them.

keyTerms.meaning: His youth (his early period of life) was becoming, meaning proper
A bad reputation
His youth, his childhood

steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation is quoted in הלכה as one of the qualities looked for in a regular שליח ציבור.

phrases.english: 'And his youth was becoming'
phrases.notes: Quoting the next quality in רבי יהודה's list

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא עָלָיו שֵׁם רַע בְּיַלְדוּתוֹ.
phrases.english: This is one about whom no bad name went out during his youth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the next phrase in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'His youth was becoming' means he never had a bad reputation in his youth.

steps.title: What does 'she gave her voice against me' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in ירמיה and asks what the phrase 'she gave her voice against me' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My heritage became to me like a lion in the forest; she gave her voice against me; therefore I hated her.' What does 'she gave her voice against me' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק and asks what it means. It is setting up the next step, which will connect the פסוק to the שליח ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, הקב"ה says He 'hated' His people because of a 'voice' raised against Him. The גמרא wants to know what kind of voice could cause such a strong reaction.

keyTerms.meaning: My heritage, meaning כלל ישראל
Like a lion in the forest
I hated her
What is? (asking for the meaning of something)

phrases.english: 'My heritage has become to me like a lion in the forest;'

phrases.aramaic: נָתְנָה עָלַי בְּקוֹלָהּ עַל כֵּן שְׂנֵאתִיהָ״,
phrases.english: she has given her voice against me; therefore I have hated her.'
What is the meaning of 'she has given her voice against me'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related פסוק that connects to the topic of who is fit to be a שליח ציבור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose 'voice' the פסוק is describing, that causes God to 'hate' it.

steps.title: The unworthy שליח ציבור
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק refers to an unworthy שליח ציבור who goes up to lead the תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב, and some say רבי חמא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: This is an unworthy שליח ציבור who goes down before the תיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'voice' in the פסוק is the voice of a שליח ציבור who is not fit for the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an unworthy person prays for the community, his voice does not bring God closer. Instead, it is described as something God 'hates.' This shows why the qualities listed earlier really matter.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (introducing a different version of who said it)
The person leading the prayer for the community
Worthy, fit
Who goes down before the ark, meaning who leads the prayer

steps.whatToRemember: The fast-day שליח ציבור must be truly worthy: poor and praying from the heart, free of sin, and with a clean reputation from his youth. An unworthy one is what the פסוק calls a 'voice' God hates.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Mar Zutra bar Toviyah said in the name of Rav,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Chama said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
phrases.notes: Two versions of the chain of transmission

phrases.english: This is a prayer leader who is not worthy
who goes down before the ark.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר שֶׁאֵינוֹ הָגוּן הַיּוֹרֵד לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'voice' is an unworthy שליח ציבור leading the prayer.

steps.title: The משנה: twenty-four ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: on a fast day the שליח ציבור says 24 ברכות, the regular 18 plus six more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he says before them twenty-four blessings: the eighteen of every day, and he adds another six to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the words of the משנה about how many ברכות the fast-day תפילה has. It is setting up a question about this count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's math is simple: 18 regular ברכות plus 6 extra equals 24. The next step will challenge whether the extra number is really six.

keyTerms.meaning: Blessings
Eighteen, meaning the regular עמידה said every day
He adds

phrases.english: And he recites before them twenty-four blessings:
the eighteen of every day,
and he adds to them another six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast-day תפילה has 24 ברכות: the regular 18 plus six added ones.

steps.title: Aren't there seven added ברכות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה elsewhere speaks of a 'seventh' added ברכה, which suggests seven additions, not six.
steps.simpleTranslation: These six — they are seven! As we learned: On the seventh he says, 'Blessed is He Who has mercy on the land'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the number six by quoting a later line of the משנה that mentions a 'seventh' ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה lists a 'seventh' ending, then it seems there are seven added ברכות, making 25 in total, not 24. The two statements in the משנה seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: These
They are
As we learned in a משנה
Who has mercy on the land, the ending of the last fast-day ברכה

phrases.english: These six — they are seven!
As we learned in the mishnah: On the seventh he says,
'Blessed is He Who has mercy on the land'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count of six stated in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that six ברכות are added
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another line of the משנה refers to a 'seventh' added ברכה, implying seven additions, which contradicts the number six.

steps.title: 'Seventh' counts the lengthened ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'seventh' counts the regular ברכה of גואל ישראל, which is only lengthened, not newly added.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What does 'seventh' mean? Seventh counting the lengthened one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the contradiction. The list of seven endings includes one ברכה that already exists in the daily עמידה and is just made longer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ending in the משנה's list is really גואל ישראל, one of the regular 18, but extended on a fast day. So only six ברכות are truly new, and the total stays 24. The word 'seventh' just counts that lengthened ברכה along with the new ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Seventh
For the long one, meaning counting the lengthened ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think there really are seven new ברכות. One of the seven endings belongs to a regular ברכה (גואל ישראל) that is only made longer, so the total is still 24.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
What is 'seventh'? Seventh counting the lengthened one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting how the count is made
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Seventh' means there are seven brand-new ברכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Seventh' includes one existing ברכה that is lengthened, so only six are new.

steps.title: ברייתא: גואל ישראל is lengthened
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן בר יצחק: on a fast day the ברכה of גואל ישראל is lengthened and given a special ending, followed by תקיעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: In 'גואל ישראל' he lengthens, and at its ending he says: 'He Who answered אברהם on הר המוריה, He will answer you and hear the sound of your cry on this day. Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel.' And they answer 'אמן' after him, and the חזן הכנסת says to them: 'Blow, sons of אהרן, blow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that proves the ברכה of גואל ישראל is made longer on a fast day, just as רב נחמן בר יצחק said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says clearly 'in גואל ישראל he lengthens,' which shows that a regular ברכה is extended, not replaced. This confirms that one of the seven endings is a lengthened old ברכה. The ברייתא also describes the community answering אמן and the כהנים blowing the trumpets.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
He lengthens
Its ending, the closing line of the ברכה
The attendant of the shul
Blow (the trumpets)

steps.whatToRemember: The fast-day תפילה has 24 ברכות. The regular ברכה of גואל ישראל is lengthened with 'מי שענה את אברהם בהר המוריה,' and six new ברכות are added. Together these make the 'seven' endings listed in the משנה.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: In 'Redeemer of Israel' he lengthens,
and at its ending he says:
'He Who answered Avraham on Mount Moriah,'

phrases.aramaic: הוּא יַעֲנֶה אֶתְכֶם וְיִשְׁמַע בְּקוֹל צַעֲקַתְכֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה.
phrases.english: He will answer you and hear the sound of your cry on this day.
Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel.'
And they answer 'Amen' after him,
and the synagogue attendant says to them:
'Blow, sons of Aharon, blow!'
phrases.notes: The כהנים blow the trumpets after this ברכה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports the answer in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that one of the seven endings is a lengthened regular ברכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the ברכה of גואל ישראל is lengthened on a fast day

steps.title: The second added blessing and the alternating blasts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The שליח ציבור says the second added ברכה, ending זוכר הנשכחות. The people answer אמן, and the חזן הכנסת calls out 'הריעו'. After each ברכה the call switches between תקיעה and תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he goes on and says: 'The One Who answered our forefathers at ים סוף, He will answer you and hear the sound of your cry today. Blessed… Who remembers the forgotten.' They answer 'אמן' after him. The חזן הכנסת tells them: 'Sound a תרועה, sons of אהרן, sound a תרועה!' The same goes for every ברכה: after one he says 'Blow a תקיעה,' and after the next he says 'Sound a תרועה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going. It describes the second added fast-day ברכה and the pattern of blasts that follows each ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 covered the first of the seven endings, the lengthened גואל ישראל, which was followed by a call for תקיעה. Here the next ending, זוכר הנשכחות, is followed by a call for תרועה. From here on the two kinds of blast simply take turns, one ברכה after another.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who remembers the forgotten' – the ending of the second added ברכה (זכרונות)
The synagogue attendant, who calls out instructions to the כהנים
'Sound a תרועה' – broken, wavering blasts
'Blow a תקיעה' – one long, steady blast
With each and every ברכה

phrases.english: And he goes back and says:
phrases.notes: The שליח ציבור continues to the next added ברכה

phrases.aramaic: ״מִי שֶׁעָנָה אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ עַל יַם סוּף,
phrases.english: "He Who answered our forefathers at the Red Sea,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day,
Blessed… Who remembers the forgotten."
phrases.notes: The ending of the second added ברכה

phrases.english: And they answer "Amen" after him,
and the synagogue attendant says to them:
"Sound a teruah, sons of Aaron, sound a teruah!"
phrases.notes: After the first ברכה it was תקיעה; now it is תרועה

phrases.english: And so too with each and every blessing:
after one he says: "Blow a tekiah,"
and after the next he says: "Sound a teruah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 9 and describes the next ברכה and the blast pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each added fast-day ברכה is answered with אמן and followed by a blast, alternating between תקיעה and תרועה.

steps.title: This procedure applies only outside the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits what it just described. The אמן-and-blast procedure is only for the places outside the מקדש (גבולין). In the מקדש it is done differently, because people do not answer אמן there.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? Outside the מקדש. But in the מקדש it is not done this way, because people do not answer 'אמן' in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא narrows the procedure it just described. It says it applies only outside the מקדש, because in the מקדש nobody answers אמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase במה דברים אמורים is a standard way to limit the rule just stated. The order of ברכות and blasts is still the fast-day service everywhere. The only difference in the מקדש is how the people respond to the ברכות, since אמן is not used there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When does this apply?' – a formula that limits a rule
'Borders' – everywhere outside the מקדש
The בית המקדש, the Temple
One does not answer אמן

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean there is no fast-day service with ברכות and blasts in the מקדש. Only the people's response is different: no אמן.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
In the outlying areas (outside the Temple),
but in the Temple it is not so,
because one does not answer "Amen" in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the procedure of step 10 to places outside the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אמן-based procedure applies only outside the מקדש. In the מקדש, אמן is not answered.

steps.title: What is the source that אמן is not said in the מקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source of the claim that אמן is not answered in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that people do not answer 'אמן' in the מקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short question that sets up the next step. It asks where we learn that אמן is not said in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 stated the rule without giving a source. This question is not an attack on the rule. It just asks for the פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And from where do we know?' – a request for a source

phrases.english: And from where do we know that one does not answer "Amen" in the Temple?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that אמן is not answered in the מקדש.

steps.title: Derivation from the פסוק in נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in נחמיה says 'exalted above all blessing and praise'. This teaches that every ברכה must get its own praise. So in the מקדש a simple אמן, the same short answer for every ברכה, is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Stand up and bless ה׳ your God from forever to forever, and let them bless Your glorious Name, which is exalted above every blessing and praise.' You might think that all the ברכות together get just one kind of praise. So the פסוק says 'exalted above every blessing and praise': for every ברכה, give Him a praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. It brings a פסוק from נחמיה and explains how it shows that the מקדש needs more than אמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the פסוק, we might think one standard reply, like אמן, is fine for every ברכה. The words 'על כל ברכה ותהלה' are read as 'for each ברכה, its own praise'. So in the מקדש each ברכה gets a full praise instead of a plain אמן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it is said' – introduces a פסוק
'One might think' – introduces a wrong first assumption
'The פסוק teaches' – introduces the correct reading
Praise
'Exalted above every blessing' – the key words of the derivation

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the response ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד in the מקדש instead of אמן. That difference between the מקדש and everywhere else shows up in several places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: As it is said:
"Stand up, bless the Lord your God
from everlasting to everlasting,
and let them bless Your glorious Name
that is exalted above all blessing and praise."
One might think that for all the blessings together
there should be only one praise,
phrases.notes: That is, one uniform response such as אמן

phrases.english: therefore the verse teaches:
"exalted above all blessing and praise" —

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל בְּרָכָה תֵּן לוֹ תְּהִלָּה.
phrases.english: for every blessing, give Him a praise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נחמיה ט:ה ('על כל ברכה ותהלה') teaches that every ברכה needs its own praise, so a plain אמן is not used in the מקדש.

steps.title: What is said in the מקדש instead?
steps.stepSummary: If אמן is not said in the מקדש, the ברייתא asks what the שליח ציבור actually says there.
steps.simpleTranslation: So then, in the מקדש, what does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. Now that we know the מקדש is different, it asks what the actual wording there is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11–13 only told us what is not done in the מקדש. This question asks for the positive version: what the ending of the ברכה and the people's response sound like there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So then' – moves to the follow-up question
'What does he say?'

phrases.english: So then, in the Temple, what does he say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the rule that אמן is not used in the מקדש and asks for the replacement wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of the ברכה and the response in the מקדש.

steps.title: The מקדש wording and response
steps.stepSummary: In the מקדש the ברכה ends with a longer phrase: 'ברוך ה׳ אלהי ישראל מן העולם ועד העולם, ברוך גואל ישראל'. The people answer ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד, and the חזן הכנסת calls the כהנים to blow a תקיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, from forever to forever. Blessed… Who redeems Israel.' They answer after him: 'Blessed is the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.' And the חזן הכנסת tells them: 'Blow, כהנים, sons of אהרן, blow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the actual wording used in the מקדש. It replaces the ending and the people's אמן with longer praises, then gives the call to blow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This puts step 13 into practice. The ending gets the extra words 'מן העולם ועד העולם', and the people's reply is the full praise ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו instead of a short אמן. The call to blow is still made, now addressed specifically to 'the כהנים'. The text continues next.

keyTerms.term: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
keyTerms.meaning: 'Blessed is the Name of His glorious kingdom forever' – the response used in the מקדש instead of אמן
'Redeemer of Israel' – the ending of the first fast-day ברכה
The כהנים, sons of Aharon, who blow the trumpets

steps.whatToRemember: Outside the מקדש, each fast-day ברכה is answered with אמן. In the מקדש, the ending is longer and the people answer ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד, based on 'על כל ברכה ותהלה'. In both places the blasts alternate between תקיעה and תרועה.

phrases.english: "Blessed is the Lord, God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.
Blessed… Redeemer of Israel."
And they answer after him:
"Blessed is the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
And the synagogue attendant says to them:
"Blow, priests, sons of Aaron, blow!"

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרוּךְ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִן הָעוֹלָם וְעַד הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with the actual wording used in the מקדש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the מקדש the ending is 'ברוך ה׳ אלהי ישראל מן העולם ועד העולם, ברוך גואל ישראל', the response is ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד, and the כהנים are called to blow.

steps.title: The second blessing and the pattern for all the rest
steps.stepSummary: The שליח ציבור says the second added ברכה, ending with 'מי שענה את אברהם בהר המוריה' and 'זוכר הנשכחות'. The people answer ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו, and the חזן הכנסת calls 'הריעו'. This pattern repeats for every ברכה, switching between תקעו and הריעו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he says the next ברכה: 'He Who answered אברהם on הר המוריה will answer you and hear your cry today. Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, Who remembers the forgotten.' The people answer 'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever.' The חזן הכנסת says: 'Blast, כהנים, sons of אהרן, blast!' The same happens after every ברכה. After one he says 'Blow' and after the next he says 'Blast', until he finishes them all.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps describing the מקדש procedure from step 15. Now it gives the second ברכה and the repeating pattern for all the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each added ברכה ends with a 'מי שענה' line about someone ה׳ answered in the past, here אברהם at the עקידה. In the מקדש, the people answer with ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו instead of אמן. The calls to the כהנים alternate: one ברכה gets a תקיעה, the next gets a תרועה.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes back and says (continues with the next blessing)
Mount Moriah, where the עקידה took place
Who remembers the forgotten (the ending of this blessing)
The synagogue attendant who directs the service
Blow! (a long, straight sound, a תקיעה)
Blast! (a broken, wavering sound, a תרועה)

phrases.english: And he goes back and says:
"He Who answered Abraham on Mount Moriah,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.
Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel,
Who remembers the forgotten."
And they answer after him:
"Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
And the synagogue attendant says to them:
"Blast, priests, sons of Aaron, blast, etc."
And so too with each and every blessing:
after one he says "Blow"
and after the next he says "Blast",
until he finishes all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the מקדש procedure begun in step 15, now for the second ברכה and the rest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the מקדש, each added ברכה gets ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו from the people and a call to the כהנים, alternating between תקיעה and תרועה until all are done.
steps.whatToRemember: In the מקדש: no אמן. Instead the people say ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו, and the כהנים blow, switching between תקיעה and תרועה.

steps.title: Two רבנן used this procedure in their towns
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלפתא in צפורי and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון in סיכני brought this procedure into their towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the custom that רבי חלפתא set up in צפורי, and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון in סיכני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that two great רבנן used this מקדש-style procedure outside the מקדש. This sets up the reaction of the חכמים in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the procedure was described as the way things were done in the מקדש. Here we learn it was actually practiced in two towns far from the מקדש. That raises an obvious question: was this allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: Set up a custom, made it the practice
A תנא, father of רבי יוסי
Tzippori, a city in the Galilee
A תנא, later one of the עשרה הרוגי מלכות
Sikhni, a town in the Galilee

phrases.english: And this is the custom Rabbi Ḥalafta established in Tzippori,
and Rabbi Ḥananya ben Teradyon in Sikhni.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports that the procedure just described was put into practice outside the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון practiced the ברוך שם and blowing procedure in their towns.

steps.title: The חכמים limit the custom to the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: When the matter came before the חכמים, they said this procedure was only done at the שערי מזרח and on the הר הבית, not in other towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the matter came before the חכמים, they said: They only acted this way at the שערי מזרח and on the הר הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים respond to the custom of רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון. They say it belongs only in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not say the procedure itself is wrong. They say it fits only one place, the מקדש area. Bringing it into regular towns is a mistake, because outside the מקדש people answer אמן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority of the רבנן)
Were accustomed to do, practiced
The Eastern Gates of the מקדש
The Temple Mount

phrases.english: And when the matter came before the Sages,
they said: They did not act this way
except at the Eastern Gates and on the Temple Mount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects using the custom from step 17 outside the מקדש.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the מקדש procedure in towns outside the מקדש. The procedure itself is accepted for the מקדש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The procedure belongs to the מקדש only. Moving it to the גבולין puts it in the wrong place.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ברוך שם response and the alternating blowing are specific to the מקדש, which the ברייתא in the following steps explains.

steps.title: A second version: the custom followed another ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some say the custom followed a different ברייתא. In that ברייתא, the שליח ציבור says twenty-four ברכות: the usual שמונה עשרה plus six more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say it was as taught in a ברייתא: He says twenty-four blessings before them, the eighteen of every day, and adds six more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another opinion ('some say') about what the custom was, based on a different ברייתא. This step starts quoting that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Some say' brings a second version of the ברייתא that describes the fast-day order. It opens with the same count as the משנה: 18 regular ברכות plus 6 extra make 24. It then sets out the difference between the גבולין and the מקדש in its own words, ending with the פסוק in step 25. After that, a separate ברייתא introduced by תנו רבנן (steps 26-30) describes the מקדש order and ends with the report about רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (introduces another version)
As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
Twenty-four blessings
The eighteen blessings of the daily עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: From here to step 30, the גמרא repeats material very similar to steps 9-18. You have not lost your place. Steps 19-25 are the 'some say' version of the ברייתא. Steps 26-30 are another ברייתא, introduced by תנו רבנן, that covers the מקדש order again.

phrases.english: And some say: as it was taught in a baraita:
He says before them twenty-four blessings:
the eighteen of every day,
and he adds to them another six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a second, fuller version of the ברייתא quoted in steps 9-18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a תענית צבור the שליח ציבור says 24 ברכות: the regular 18 plus 6 added ones.

steps.title: Where do the six extra blessings go?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where in the עמידה the six added ברכות are placed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And those six, where does he say them?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a simple clarifying question: at what point in the עמידה are the six extra ברכות inserted? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing there are six extra ברכות is not enough. We also need to know where they fit in the order of the עמידה.

keyTerms.meaning: Those six (the added blessings)
Where?
Says them

phrases.english: And those six, where does he say them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the placement of the six ברכות mentioned in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The location in the עמידה of the six added ברכות.

steps.title: Between גואל and רופא, with אמן in the גבולין
steps.stepSummary: The six go between גואל ישראל and רופא חולי. He lengthens the ברכה of גאולה, and the people answer אמן after every ברכה. This was the practice in the גבולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between 'Redeemer' and 'Healer of the sick'. He lengthens the redemption blessing, and they answer 'אמן' after each and every blessing. This was the custom outside the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: the extra ברכות go right after גואל ישראל. It also explains that outside the מקדש the people answer אמן to each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה of גאולה is stretched out, and the six extra ברכות are attached there before רופא חולי. In the גבולין the response to each ברכה is a simple אמן. This is the key difference from the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה of גואל ישראל, Redeemer of Israel
The ברכה of רופא חולי עמו ישראל, Healer of the sick
Lengthens
The response affirming a blessing
Places outside the מקדש

phrases.english: Between "Redeemer" and "Healer of the sick,"
and he lengthens the redemption blessing,
and they answer "amen" after him
on each and every blessing.
And this is how they practiced in the outlying areas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 and adds the גבולין response of אמן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The six go between גואל and רופא חולי, inside a lengthened גאולה ברכה, and in the גבולין each ברכה is answered with אמן.

steps.title: In the מקדש: a longer ending and no אמן
steps.stepSummary: In the מקדש the ending was 'ברוך ה׳ אלהי ישראל מן העולם ועד העולם, ברוך גואל ישראל', and the people did not answer אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the מקדש they would say: 'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel.' And they did not answer 'אמן' after him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא contrasts the מקדש with the גבולין. In the מקדש the ending is longer and nobody answers אמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבל marks the switch from the גבולין to the מקדש. The ending of the ברכה becomes grander ('from everlasting to everlasting'), and the simple אמן disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple
From everlasting to everlasting
Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel

phrases.english: But in the Temple, they would say:
"Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.
Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel."
And they would not answer "amen" after him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the מקדש practice with the גבולין practice of step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the מקדש the ברכה ends with a longer formula and the people do not answer אמן.

steps.title: Why the difference: no אמן in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the practice differs so much and answers that אמן is not said in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all this? Because one does not answer 'אמן' in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks itself why the מקדש is so different and answers right away: אמן is not said there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question and answer come together in one line. Everything about the מקדש procedure depends on one rule: there is no אמן in the מקדש. That rule explains the longer ending and the different response.

keyTerms.meaning: And why all this? (why such a big difference)
Because
Answer, respond

phrases.english: And why all this?
Because one does not answer "amen" in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the מקדש practice in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference exists because אמן is not answered in the מקדש.

steps.title: What is the source that no אמן is said in the מקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source of the rule that אמן is not said in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that one does not answer 'אמן' in the מקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for a source for the rule it just stated. This sets up the פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule this specific needs a basis in a פסוק. The ברייתא now looks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we know)?
That one does not
In the Temple

phrases.english: And from where do we know that one does not answer "amen" in the Temple?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that אמן is not answered in the מקדש.

steps.title: The פסוק in נחמיה: every blessing needs its own praise
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in נחמיה says ה׳'s name is 'exalted above all blessing and praise'. This teaches that each ברכה must get its own praise, so a plain אמן is not enough in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Stand up and bless ה׳ your God from everlasting to everlasting, and let them bless Your glorious Name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise.' This means: for each and every blessing, give Him praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a פסוק from נחמיה and explains what it teaches. This finishes the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'על כל ברכה ותהלה' are read as 'for every ברכה, a praise'. In the מקדש, each ברכה deserves its own full praise, such as ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו, not the same short אמן every time.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
Stand up and bless
And is exalted
Praise
Give Him

steps.whatToRemember: No אמן in the מקדש, because the פסוק teaches that every ברכה must get its own praise. In the גבולין, אמן is said after each ברכה.

phrases.english: As it is said: "Stand up and bless ה׳ your God
from everlasting to everlasting,
and let them bless Your glorious Name,
which is exalted above all blessing and praise" —

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה תֵּן לוֹ תְּהִלָּה.
phrases.english: for each and every blessing, give Him praise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source requested in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נחמיה 9:5, read as requiring a separate praise for every ברכה, which rules out a simple אמן in the מקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for answering ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו instead of אמן in the מקדש, a difference that shaped the whole תענית procedure there.

steps.title: The first ברכה in the מקדש and the call to blow
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes the first added ברכה in the מקדש. The ending is said, the people answer ״ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו״, the חזן calls ״תקעו כהנים תקעו״, the ״מי שענה את אברהם״ line is said, and the כהנים blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: At the first ברכה he says, 'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, from forever to forever. Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel.' The people answer, 'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.' The חזן הכנסת says, 'Blow, כהנים, blow!' Then he goes on: 'He Who answered אברהם on הר המוריה will answer you and hear your cry today.' Then they blow a long blast, a broken blast, and a long blast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out, step by step, what happened in the מקדש at the first added ברכה of the fast-day תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fills in the picture from steps 22-25. Since אמן is not said in the מקדש, the people answer with the longer praise ״ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד״. After that response, the שופר blowing is tied to the ברכה through the חזן's call and the ״מי שענה״ line.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)

keyTerms.term: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
keyTerms.meaning: Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever (the response used in the מקדש instead of אמן)
The synagogue attendant who directed the order of the service
They blow a תקיעה, a long, steady blast
They blow a תרועה, a broken, wavering blast

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two calls. ״תקעו״ means a set that starts and ends with a long תקיעה. Later, ״הריעו״ means a set that starts and ends with a broken תרועה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
At the first blessing he says:
'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel,
from forever to forever.
Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel.'
And they answer after him:
'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.'
And the synagogue attendant says:
'Blow, priests, blow!'
And he goes back and says:
'He Who answered Abraham on Mount Moriah,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day.'
And they blow a long blast, a broken blast, and a long blast.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows in practice what replaced אמן in the מקדש, which step 25 just explained
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the מקדש, after the first added ברכה, the people answered ״ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו״. Then the כהנים blew תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה at the call ״תקעו״.

steps.title: The second blessing and the call for a broken blast
steps.stepSummary: For the second ברכה the ending is ״זוכר הנשכחות״. The same response follows. The חזן calls ״הריעו בני אהרן הריעו״, the ״מי שענה את אבותינו על ים סוף״ line is said, and they blow תרועה-תקיעה-תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the second ברכה he says, 'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, from forever to forever. Blessed is the One Who remembers forgotten things.' The people answer, 'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.' The חזן הכנסת says, 'Sound the broken blast, sons of אהרן, sound it!' Then he says, 'He Who answered our fathers at ים סוף will answer you and hear your cry today.' Then they blow a broken blast, a long blast, and a broken blast.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and describes the second ברכה. This time the order of the blasts is flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setup is the same as the first ברכה, but two things change. The ending is now ״זוכר הנשכחות״, and the call is ״הריעו״. Because of that call, the set starts and ends with a תרועה instead of a תקיעה.

keyTerms.meaning: The One Who remembers forgotten things (ending of the second added ברכה)
Sound a תרועה (a broken blast)!
Sons of Aaron, meaning the כהנים
The Red Sea

phrases.english: And at the second blessing he says:
'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel,
from forever to forever.
Blessed is the One Who remembers forgotten things.'
And they answer after him:
'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.'
And the synagogue attendant says:
'Sound the broken blast, sons of Aaron, sound it!'
And he says:

phrases.aramaic: ״מִי שֶׁעָנָה אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ עַל יַם סוּף,
phrases.english: 'He Who answered our fathers at the Red Sea,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day.'
And they blow a broken blast, a long blast, and a broken blast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the second ברכה and flips the order of the blasts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the second ברכה the call is ״הריעו״, and the blasts are תרועה-תקיעה-תרועה.

steps.title: The pattern switches for every blessing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the general rule. The calls switch between ״תקעו״ and ״הריעו״ for each ברכה until all the ברכות are finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it goes for every single blessing. At one he says 'Blow,' and at the next he says 'Sound the broken blast,' until he finishes all the blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of listing every ברכה one by one, the ברייתא gives the rule: keep switching back and forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 26 and 27 were two examples. This line turns them into a pattern for all the added ברכות. Odd ברכות get ״תקעו״ and even ברכות get ״הריעו״.

keyTerms.meaning: At each and every blessing
Until he finishes

steps.whatToRemember: In the מקדש, every added ברכה was answered with ״ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו״ and followed by שופר blasts. The calls switched between ״תקעו״ and ״הריעו״.

phrases.english: And so it is with every single blessing.
At one he says 'Blow,'
and at the next he says 'Sound the broken blast,'
until he finishes all the blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the two examples into a general rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The calls switch between ״תקעו״ and ״הריעו״ for every ברכה through the end.

steps.title: Two רבנן set up this practice in their towns
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reports that רבי חלפתא in ציפורי and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון in סיכני led their communities in this מקדש-style practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is how רבי חלפתא led the practice in ציפורי, and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון in סיכני.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us that two Sages brought this מקדש order into their own towns, outside the מקדש. This sets up the חכמים' reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the order was described as a מקדש practice. Here two leaders used it in the גבולין, in ordinary towns. That raises the question whether this is allowed, which the next line answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Led the people in, set up as a practice
ציפורי (Tzippori), a city in the Galil
סיכני (Sikhni), a town in the Galil

phrases.english: And this is how Rabbi Ḥalafta led the practice in Tzippori,
and Rabbi Ḥananya ben Teradyon in Sikhni.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports that the מקדש order was used outside the מקדש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון used this order in their own towns.

steps.title: The חכמים limit this practice to the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: When the matter reached the חכמים, they said this order was done only at the Eastern Gates and on the הר הבית, not in ordinary towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the matter came before the חכמים, they said: This practice was done only at the שערי מזרח and on the הר הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים respond to what רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון did. They rule that this special order belongs only in the area of the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the ברייתא's topic. The ״ברוך שם״ response and the כהנים blowing after each ברכה are a מקדש-only practice, which is why the מקדש and the גבולין differ (steps 21-23). Outside the מקדש, the regular order with אמן stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: The Eastern Gates of the Temple Mount
The Temple Mount
Practice, do as a custom

steps.whatToRemember: The ״ברוך שם״ and שופר order after each ברכה was only for the מקדש area. The חכמים did not accept it in ordinary towns.

phrases.english: And when the matter came before the Sages, they said:
They did not practice this way
except at the Eastern Gates and on the Temple Mount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects using the practice from step 29 outside the מקדש
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The special order of ״ברוך שם״ plus שופר blasts was only for the Eastern Gates and the הר הבית.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי יהודה, who says the leader did not need to say זכרונות and שופרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He did not need to say the זכרונות and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It is setting up a discussion of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed זכרונות and שופרות among the added ברכות of a fast day. רבי יהודה disagrees and says they were not needed. Instead, other passages about famine and suffering were said.

keyTerms.meaning: Remembrances, the passages about ה׳ remembering
And so on (short for the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זִכְרוֹנוֹת כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: He did not need to say Remembrances, and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זִכְרוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מקדש topic and quotes a new line from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, זכרונות and שופרות were not said on a fast day.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אדא דמן יפו asks why רבי יהודה holds that זכרונות and שופרות are not said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אדא from יפו said: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אדא דמן יפו asks for the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's view. He is setting up his own answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה gave a ruling without a reason. This question asks for the logic, so we understand why these ברכות are left out on a fast day.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
From יפו (Jaffa)

phrases.english: Rabbi Adda from Jaffa said:
What is Rabbi Yehuda's reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling quoted in step 31
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה holds that זכרונות and שופרות are not said on a fast day

steps.title: These passages are said only at certain times
steps.stepSummary: רבי אדא begins his answer: זכרונות and שופרות are said only at certain times. The answer finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because זכרונות and שופרות are not said (except at certain times, which the next amud lists).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אדא starts to give רבי יהודה's reason. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that זכרונות and שופרות have their own set times. Since a fast day is not one of those times, רבי יהודה leaves them out.

keyTerms.meaning: Because one does not say
שופרות, the passages about the שופר

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished yet. Do not read it as 'זכרונות and שופרות are never said.' The next part names the specific times when they are said.

phrases.english: Because Remembrances and Shofarot are not said (continues in the next part)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to step 32's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זכרונות and שופרות are said only at specific times, and a fast day is not one of them (the list continues on the next amud).
